items.author: zenkaixbt
items.context: zenkaixbt: el próximo halving es en 507 días; afirma que 'históricamente siempre funcionó' comprar BTC 500 días antes del halving y vender 500 días después. Post de hace ~20 min con 35 likes y 24 respuestas.
items.suggested_text:
Four halvings is a small sample, and "always" carries a lot of weight in that sentence. The mechanism behind it is real, though: the next halving cuts the block subsidy from 3.125 to 1.5625 BTC, so new supply drops from ~450 to ~225 BTC a day, and by then only 3.125% of the 21M will be left to issue.

What changed is who sits on the other side of that trade. In 2012 and 2016, miner selling was a big share of daily flow; today spot ETFs and corporate treasuries can absorb or dump several days' worth of issuance in a single session. The supply shock shrinks every cycle in absolute terms, while demand gets harder to read.

The calendar still matters. Maybe just not in the way a 500-day rule assumes.
